body_text: Looking for a way to make extra money on the weekend? Weekend jobs are a great option if you want flexible hours, quick cash, or a way to build new skills without committing to a full-time role. Many businesses are busiest on Saturdays and Sundays, which means more shifts, higher demand, and often better pay. Here are some of the best weekend jobs and why they’re worth considering. What's a good weekend job? A good weekend job offers flexible hours, quick onboarding, and steady pay without long-term commitments. Popular options include warehouse shifts, event staffing, hospitality roles, delivery driving, and gig-based work. These jobs are ideal for students, part-time workers, or anyone looking to earn extra income on Saturdays and Sundays while keeping their weekday schedule open. Top 10 Weekend Jobs 1. Work a shift with Instawork This is one of the most flexible ways to work weekends. You can pick up shifts in hospitality, warehouses, and events without committing to a long-term schedule. You get fast pay and full control over when you work. Find Weekend Jobs With the Instawork App Find flexible shifts, earn money on your schedule, and work when you want. 2. Work weekend nights at Bloomingdale’s Retail stores are busiest on weekends, and Bloomingdale’s offers employee discounts, which makes this job attractive if you enjoy fashion and customer service. Helpful link: bloomingdales.com 3. Test apps App testing lets you earn money by finding bugs and giving feedback on new software. You can usually work from home and choose flexible projects. Useful resources: UserTesting , Test IO , uTest 4. Work at a movie theatre Theatres are busiest on weekends, so shifts are easy to get. Many locations offer free movies, popcorn, and drinks as perks. Helpful link: careers.amctheatres.com 5. Work as a tour guide Tour guides are in high demand on weekends when most people travel. It’s a great job if you like talking to people and sharing local knowledge. Helpful platforms: Airbnb Experiences , GetYourGuide 6. Wait tables at a restaurant Weekend shifts usually mean more customers and higher tips. It’s one of the fastest ways to make good cash in just two days of work. 7. Bartend at a hotel Hotel bars get busy with guests and events on weekends. With some training or experience, bartending can be very rewarding and high-paying. Helpful resource: bartender schools or local hospitality training centers 8. Work as a delivery driver Weekend demand for food and packages is high. Some drivers make close to full-time income working only Fridays through Sundays. Helpful link: Amazon Flex Weekend job working as a delivery driver 9. Work through TaskRabbit TaskRabbit lets you choose short jobs like moving, cleaning, or assembly. You only work when you want and set your own availability. Helpful link: taskrabbit.com/become-a-tasker 10. Babysit elementary-aged kids ‍ Weekend babysitting is popular with parents who want time off or date nights. Once families trust you, they often book recurring work. How to Get a Weekend Job The fastest way to land a weekend-only job is to go in person. Bring a printed resume and explain clearly that you’re looking for weekend-only work. Build rapport with employees when you visit. Let them know you’re open to weekends and ask if they can pass your resume to a manager or HR. Full-time staff often prefer weekdays, so managers are usually happy to hire people who specifically want weekend shifts. Highest Paying Weekend Jobs When people think of weekend work, they often imagine lower-paid roles like retail or entry-level hospitality. But many weekend gigs pay well above average , especially once you factor in tips or demand spikes on Saturdays and Sundays. Delivery & Rideshare Driving Driving for food delivery services (like DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub) or rideshare platforms can be lucrative on weekend nights and busy afternoons — many workers report significantly higher earnings due to peak demand and tips, often $15–$30+ per hour before expenses. Bartending & Event Service Work Bartenders at busy weekend venues often earn a modest base wage but make the bulk of their income from tips , which can push effective earnings well above typical hourly rates — especially at private events or high-traffic bars. Pet Sitting & Dog Walking Weekend schedules are ideal for pet care services. Platforms like Rover and Wag match sitters with owners, and rates typically range from $15–$50+ per hour depending on service type and location. Tutoring & Specialized Freelance Work If you have expertise in a subject area, tutoring can pay $20–$50+ per hour — especially for test prep or STEM topics. Similarly, freelance gigs like writing, design, or coding can command premium rates for weekend projects. House Cleaning & Brand Promotion Weekend house cleaners often earn $20–$50/hour , particularly for deep cleans or turnover jobs (e.g., Airbnbs). Brand ambassadors and promotional staff can also earn $18–$30+ per hour working weekend events or retail pop-ups. ‍ Where to Find Weekend Jobs Finding quality weekend jobs (especially well-paying ones) requires knowing where employers and gig platforms list them. Here are the best places to start your search: Job Boards & Aggregators General job sites like Indeed , Snagajob , and Talent.com list weekend-focused positions across industries — from hospitality to healthcare to logistics. You can filter specifically for part-time or weekend schedules . Gig & Temporary Work Apps Apps like Instawork and Indeed Flex let you book weekend shifts on demand. These platforms match you with short-term gigs — such as event work, restaurant shifts, and warehouse jobs — often with flexible scheduling and fast pay. Company Career Pages Many businesses that rely on weekend staff (retail stores, supermarkets, hospitals, and logistics firms) list openings directly on their careers pages. If you know local employers in your area, check those pages weekly because weekend roles can fill fast. Local Community Boards & Social Platforms City-specific Facebook groups, Reddit job threads, community bulletin boards, and apps like Nextdoor or Craigslist often have local gigs that don’t get posted on big job boards — these can include farmers markets, food trucks, event help, or weekend service gigs. Networking & Direct Outreach Especially for seasonal, hospitality, or service-industry weekend work, dropping off a resume in person or asking managers directly about weekend availability can be very effective. Many small businesses prefer to interview walk-ins, especially when they’re short-staffed. More Weekend Jobs 11. Work event gigs Weddings, festivals, and corporate events mostly happen on weekends. These short shifts can be fun, social, and well paid. 12. Walk dogs Dog walking is relaxing, flexible, and easy to scale. Weekends are especially busy when owners are away or busy. Helpful apps: Rover , Wag Weekend job working as a dog walker 13. Work at McDonald’s McDonald’s is known for flexible scheduling, which makes it easier to work only weekends. It offers steady hours and reliable pay. Helpful link: jobs.mchire.com 14. Sell items on eBay You can flip unused items or thrifted goods for profit. It’s a great way to make weekend income from home. Helpful link: www.ebay.com/sl/sell 15. Drive for Amazon Amazon weekend delivery routes are consistently available and pay reliably. It’s a structured gig with predictable work. Helpful link: flex.amazon.com 16. Wash dishes at a restaurant ‍ Dishwashing is always needed on busy weekend nights. The work is simple, steady, and doesn’t require customer interaction. 17. Work weekends at CVS CVS stores are good about working around your schedule. Weekend-only shifts are common and dependable. Helpful link: jobs.cvshealth.com 18. Work in retail Retail stores rely heavily on weekend staff. These jobs offer steady hours and are easy to find. 19. Do industrial maintenance work ‍ Maintenance tasks are often scheduled at night and on weekends to avoid shutting down production. These jobs usually pay more for off-hours. 20. Deliver with Uber Eats or DoorDash Weekend evenings are the busiest times for food delivery, often with bonuses and better tips. Helpful apps: DoorDash , Uber Eats 21. Work at a café Cafés are busiest during weekend brunch and mornings. These jobs are social and often come with free or discounted drinks. 22. Work at an airport Airports never close and are busy on weekends. Weekend shifts are widely available. Helpful resources: jobs with local airport authorities 23. Work at a gas station Gas stations see steady weekend traffic from travelers and locals. Shifts are stable and easy to schedule. 24. Work in warehouses or factories Warehouses often run weekend shifts with added pay incentives. These roles are ideal if you like physical, hands-on work. 25. Work at a hospital Hospitals need staff 24/7, and weekend shifts often come with higher pay rates. Helpful resources: check the careers pages of local hospitals 26. Work in In-Home Support Services (IHSS) in California IHSS is in high demand, especially for weekend shifts. You can choose clients, register in multiple counties, and access benefits. Helpful link: www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/ihss/ihss-providers/how-to-become-an-ihss-provider 27. Work for party rental companies You’ll help deliver and set up items like tents, bounce houses, tables, and chairs. It’s manual work but easy to learn. 28. Work with IATSE or stage production companies Weekend concerts and shows create strong demand for stagehands and crew. Helpful link: iatse.net 29. Work on a loading dock at night ‍ Loading docks often hire part-time weekend workers to operate forklifts and move inventory. These shifts often pay more. 30. Work seasonal attractions Jobs at mini golf courses, ice cream shops, amusement parks, and minor league sports are perfect for weekends. They’re fun and fast-paced. 31. Work backstock in a mall store This role focuses on inventory and organizing stock instead of customer service. It’s ideal if you prefer behind-the-scenes work. 32. Work at Lowe’s or Home Depot These stores are extremely busy with weekend DIY customers and often hire weekend-only staff. Helpful links: talent.lowes.com, careers.homedepot.com 33. Work at a grocery store Grocery stores are busiest on weekends, making it easy to secure steady weekend shifts. 34. Work as a museum visitor services attendant Museums are busiest on weekends, and the work environment is calm and interesting. 35. Work at a homeless shelter Shelters often offer union jobs, flexible casual roles, and strong starting wages. Weekend availability is highly valued. 36. Work in public health services Public health departments and outreach programs sometimes need weekend workers for clinics or community support. 37. Work as a tutor Many students book weekend tutoring sessions for exam prep. It’s flexible and pays well. Helpful platforms: Wyzant , Tutor.com 38. Work at a local arena ‍ Arenas hire weekend staff for concerts and sporting events. Work includes checking tickets and bags, and you can sometimes watch parts of the show. 39. Work as an exam invigilator ‍ Testing centers need supervisors to check IDs and monitor exams. The job is quiet, low-stress, and flexible. Helpful link: Pearson VUE test center jobs 40. Work as a musician Weekend gigs at restaurants, weddings, and bars can bring in great extra income, often paid the same day. Weekend job playing musical gigs 41. Work as a night auditor at a hotel Night auditors manage front desk and simple accounting during overnight shifts. Weekend nights are often quieter and easier. 42. Referee or coach youth sports Youth leagues need referees and coaches for weekend games. Refereeing usually requires less time commitment. Helpful links: local soccer associations, YMCA, or community sports leagues FAQ How to make money on weekends from home? There are several ways to earn money from home on weekends depending on your skills and availability. Common options include freelance work such as writing, graphic design, or virtual assistance, as well as remote customer support or online tutoring. You can also sell products online, manage social media for small businesses, or complete microtasks on gig platforms. Choosing flexible work that allows you to log in for a few hours on Saturday or Sunday makes it easier to generate extra income without interfering with your weekday schedule. What warehouse jobs are best for students or people looking for weekend work? Some of the best warehouse jobs for weekend workers include picking and packing orders, sorting packages, loading and unloading trucks, and inventory counting. These roles typically offer flexible shifts and do not always require prior experience, making them ideal for students or people looking to earn extra cash on weekends. Many warehouses also offer short shifts during busy periods, which allows workers to choose hours that fit around school or other commitments. Where should I look for weekend job opportunities? You can find weekend job opportunities on job boards, gig work platforms, and staffing apps that specialize in flexible shifts. Local businesses such as restaurants, retail stores, warehouses, and event venues often need extra help on weekends and regularly post openings online. Checking company career pages, local community groups, and job marketplaces focused on hourly work can also help you find roles that specifically offer Saturday or Sunday shifts. How to find Saturday jobs? To find Saturday jobs, start by searching job boards using filters such as “weekend,” “Saturday,” or “part-time.” Many gig platforms and staffing apps allow you to browse available shifts and choose ones that fit your schedule. Retail stores, restaurants, warehouses, and event companies often need extra staff on Saturdays, so checking listings from these industries can increase your chances of finding consistent weekend work. Where can I find weekend jobs quickly? If you need a weekend job quickly, look for platforms that offer on-demand or shift-based work. These services allow workers to apply for available shifts and start working once approved. Businesses in hospitality, retail, events, and warehousing frequently need last-minute coverage for busy weekends, which means opportunities can open up with little notice and allow you to start earning right away. How to make extra income on weekends? Making extra income on weekends usually comes down to choosing flexible work that fits your availability. Many people pick up short shifts in industries like hospitality, retail, or warehouses, while others take on freelance projects or gig work. You can also combine multiple small opportunities, such as a Saturday shift plus a few hours of online work, to increase your total earnings without committing to a full second job. What are the top sites for weekend part-time jobs? Several online platforms specialize in part-time and flexible work opportunities. Job boards, gig apps, and staffing platforms often list weekend shifts in industries such as hospitality, retail, delivery, and warehouse operations. Using platforms that focus on hourly or shift-based work can make it easier to find weekend jobs because they allow you to browse available shifts and apply quickly for roles that match your schedule.

title: Beyond Injections: How Oral GLP-1s Will Fit into Obesity Care
summary: Find out how the latest oral GLP-1s are re-shaping weight health care, how they differ from injectables, and how Omada guides members to long-term health!
body_text: April 9, 2026 Beyond Injections: How Oral GLP-1s Will Fit into Obesity Care This edition covers: The newest oral GLP-1s on the market Clinical differences between oral and injectable GLP-1s How a growing range of options is re-shaping health benefit strategies Last week, the FDA approved Lilly’s new oral GLP-1 medication, Foundayo™ (orforglipron), several months after the approval of Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy® (semaglutide) pill — the first oral GLP‑1 indicated both for weight management and for reducing cardiovascular risk in adults with obesity or overweight, and established heart disease. Although oral GLP-1s aren’t entirely new— Rybelsus ® has been used for diabetes since 2019—these advances raise important questions: How will oral GLP‑1s fit into clinical practice? Will patients shift from injections to pills? Will patient demand for GLP-1s rise more aggressively? Will patients be able to persist on oral therapies longer and achieve better results? It’s too early to know. Patient behavior is notoriously difficult to predict, and few could have anticipated the widespread enthusiasm for injectable GLP‑1s or the cultural familiarity with terms like “GLP‑1.” What I’ve learned over decades of direct patient care is that expanding therapeutic choice almost always improves engagement. When patients feel they have options, they’re more likely to start and stay with treatment. I’ve had countless conversations with patients who were reluctant to start GLP-1 therapy because of injection anxiety, access challenges, or affordability concerns. While oral GLP-1s don’t solve all of these barriers, they do provide an option for my patients who refused to try injections. As we step into a new, more accessible era of anti-obesity care, contributing to a sharper demand for GLP-1s and similar medications, it’s important that patients, providers and employers understand the key differences between formulations and how they impact health outcomes. Key Differences Between Oral and Injectable GLP-1s 1. Route of administration and lifestyle fit For patients, the biggest differences lie in how these medications fit into their current lifestyle and life stage: Oral GLP‑1s require daily dosing Injectables are once weekly but require needles Roughly one in four adults has needle aversion, and oral options may open the door for patients previously unwilling or unable to use injectables. I’ve had patients outright refuse using any type of injectable, and I’ve also had patients reluctantly agree to try an injection after receiving education and coaching. Yet, even among these patients who initially hope they’ll “get used to it,” many don’t, and later disengage from treatment. I’m grateful to finally have effective oral options for these patients because they also deserve the highest quality care. Of course, some patients don’t mind injections and may prefer a weekly dose for convenience, while others may favor a daily pill, especially if they already take other daily medications. Oral Wegovy must be taken 30 minutes before other meds, while Foundayo can be taken at any time of day. Injectables require refrigeration, which may be challenging for patients without stable housing, privacy, or climate control. Oral options avoid these barriers and may be more convenient for frequent travelers. I have patients who travel who have told me that oral options aren’t just a preference, they’re a practical necessity. 2. Desired weight‑loss magnitude Setting a realistic, healthy weight‑loss target helps determine the most appropriate therapy. I often talk to people who assume that the goal is always to lose a lot of weight as quickly as possible. Yet, this mindset leads to patients who struggle later with fatigue, excess muscle loss, or difficulty maintaining results. It’s important to set realistic and healthy goals with patients and then prescribe the most appropriate therapy and potency to the individual. For example, if I have a patient who has a BMI of 42 and multiple comorbidities, I would lean towards Zepbound, since this patient would benefit from losing at least 20% of their body weight. For patients who have weight loss goals closer to 10-15%, the Wegovy pill may provide the right balance without excessive weight reduction. I’m also increasingly mindful of sarcopenia risk. Older adults, sedentary patients, or individuals who lose weight very rapidly often do better with agents that produce more moderate weight loss, an area where emerging oral options may play an important role. 3. Long‑term use and discontinuation support A common question I get from patients is whether or not they must remain on GLP‑1s indefinitely. While I believe that obesity is a chronic condition, real‑world data suggests that many patients cannot or do not wish to stay on long‑term therapy. This underscores the need for thoughtful discontinuation strategies tailored to the patient, which can be challenging without clear guidelines or guidance from robust research studies. From the literature we do have, we know that current approaches include: Gradually reducing the dose Extending injection intervals (e.g. to every two weeks) Transitioning to non‑GLP‑1 obesity medications Oral GLP‑1s introduce new tapering pathways that may offer greater flexibility. Example: A patient who reaches their goal weight on weekly Wegovy and wishes to stop injections can consider transitioning to the Wegovy pill or Foundayo, then slowly taper the dose while monitoring weight maintenance. 4. The presence of comorbidities As we know, obesity is related to and a risk factor for a number of other cardiometabolic conditions, which means that many of my patients have multiple conditions that I need to be aware of and manage. Fortunately, GLP‑1 medications are now FDA-indicated for multiple indications beyond weight management and diabetes, including: Major cardiovascular event (heart attack and/or stroke) risk reduction in adults with cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity Metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) Moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity In practice, I select a patient’s therapy not just for weight loss, but for the total cardiometabolic profile in front of me. When one medication can address multiple conditions, it simplifies care and reduces polypharmacy. Options Drive Individualized Care for Obesity The GLP‑1 landscape is evolving rapidly, and 2026 will continue to bring an unprecedented range of options. With both injectable and oral agents available, and more coming, I see this moment not as a debate between pills and injections, but as an opportunity to individualize care more thoughtfully than ever before. For benefits leaders sifting through the growing range of GLP-1 offerings, here are three considerations to shape your strategy: How can your GLP-1 benefits package reflect the diverse needs of your population? What tools do you need to streamline and implement these therapies for your people? Which digital health providers can you partner with to ensure proper adherence and health behaviors to meaningfully reduce the risk of chronic disease? At Omada, we remain committed to guiding patients toward the medication and lifestyle approach that best supports their long‑term health, through flexible care plans and prescribing pathways. As I look toward this next era of obesity care, I’m reminded of a patient early in my career—a man who avoided treatment for years because he simply couldn’t face injections. When he finally agreed to try, he said quietly, “I just wish there were a pill.” Oral GLP-1s now deliver on that wish. They are more than a new formulation, they are a new doorway. For many patients, access begins with feeling seen and understood, and being offered choices that align with their lives. The expanding landscape of GLP‑1 therapies reinforces a simple truth: people do better when they have options. Not every patient wants the most potent medication; they want the one they can live with. Our role is to guide them with evidence, empathy, and respect for where they’re starting. Dr. Rajiv R. is a dual board-certified endocrinologist and obesity medicine specialist who has been in practice for over 20 years. He is an expert in the management of diabetes and obesity and has been recognized as one of the Top Doctors in San Diego Magazine as voted by his peers. He practices at a large multi-specialty group and regularly lectures on these conditions.

title: Garrett Showcases Electrification and Turbocharging Innovations at the Vienna Motor Symposium
summary: Garrett presents its differentiated E‑Powertrain Portfolio and Turbocharging Technologies At the 2026 Vienna Motor Symposium, Garrett Motion is showing
body_text: April 22, 2026 Garrett Showcases Electrification and Turbocharging Innovations at the Vienna Motor Symposium Garrett presents its differentiated E‑Powertrain Portfolio and Turbocharging Technologies At the 2026 Vienna Motor Symposium, Garrett Motion is showing its expanding portfolio of zero emission and emission reduction technologies, reinforcing its role in advancing efficient, scalable solutions for passenger and commercial vehicles. Garrett is presenting a range of integrated electric propulsion solutions, including a 3-in-1 E-Axle for passenger vehicles , a 2-in-1 E-Powertrain for commercial vehicles , and an E-Beam electric axle developed in collaboration with HanDe , a leading commercial vehicle axle manufacturer in China. These exhibits demonstrate Garrett’s system-level approach to electrification, integrating electric motors, power electronics and mechanical architectures to support diverse vehicle platforms and duty cycles. “Garrett is leveraging decades of expertise in high-speed turbo compressors to accelerate innovation well beyond traditional boosting applications,” said Craig Balis, Senior Vice President and Chief Technology Officer of Garrett Motion. “Our deep competencies in oil free foil bearings, high-speed electric motors, high-speed power electronics and advanced control software allow us to rapidly expand into new electrified domains while continuing to advance turbocharger performance. Mastering these technologies enables differentiated solutions that deliver efficiency, durability and scalability for our customers.” Alongside its electrified drive technologies, Garrett is also showcasing its latest generation of turbochargers and electric compressors, which have recently been launched into series production with several original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). These solutions address increasingly stringent requirements for emissions and efficiency and play a critical role in hybrid and advanced internal combustion engine platforms, where electrification and boosting technologies are increasingly combined. Garrett’s technical contribution to the symposium extends beyond product displays. Abdelhamid Bouaita, Vice President of Engineering for Zero Emissions Technologies at Garrett Motion, will present a technical paper titled ‘Leveraging high-speed electric motor technology for differentiated commercial vehicle beam axles.’ This presentation focuses on how Garrett’s high-speed motor and power electronics technologies enable compact and efficient E-Beam axle architectures that can help reduce system costs, weight and energy losses. Ultimately, this will contribute to a lower total cost of ownership (TCO) for electric commercial vehicles. Through global collaborations such as its partnership with HanDe , and by addressing both passenger and commercial vehicle applications, Garrett demonstrates its strategy of combining proven turbocharging expertise with advanced electrification technologies. This approach enables automakers and commercial vehicle manufacturers to navigate the evolving powertrain landscape while meeting regional regulatory, operational and customer requirements. Share:

title: Intensity Therapeutics Recognized with Pinnacle Award for Excellence in Healthcare Innovation
summary: Company receives the Platinum Award for Innovator in Biotech Solutions Category SHELTON, Conn., April 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Intensity…...
body_text: Company receives the Platinum Award for Innovator in Biotech Solutions Category SHELTON, Conn. , April 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Intensity Therapeutics, Inc. , (Nasdaq: INTS) ("Intensity" or the "Company"), a late-stage clinical biotechnology company focused on the discovery and development of proprietary cancer therapies using its non-covalent, drug-conjugation technology that creates drug products designed to kill tumors and increase immune system recognition of cancers, announces it has been named a winner of the 2026 Pinnacle Awards for Healthcare for its intratumoral injection platform and lead drug candidate INT230-6. The Company was selected a Platinum award winner in the Innovator in Biotech Solutions Category. INT230-6, Intensity's lead proprietary investigational product candidate, is designed for direct intratumoral injection. The drug consists of two proven, potent anti-cancer agents, cisplatin and vinblastine sulfate, and a diffusion and cell penetration enhancer molecule ("SHAO") that non-covalently conjugates to the two payload drugs, facilitating the dispersion of potent cytotoxic drugs throughout tumors and allowing the active agents to diffuse into cancer cells. INT230-6 is being developed in combination with standard-of-care therapies to improve the durability of response across multiple solid tumor indications. "The recognition from the Pinnacle Award is a testament to Intensity's commitment to changing the future of cancer care," said Intensity Therapeutics Co-Founder and CEO Lewis H. Bender. "INT230-6 represents a new, unique methodology for cancer cell death that holds the potential to shift the cancer treatment from a short-term death sentence to chronic diseases, even for malignancies that are unresponsive to immunotherapy." The Pinnacle Awards is an esteemed annual awards program dedicated to recognizing and celebrating outstanding achievements across various industries. Its mission is to honor companies, products, and individuals that have demonstrated exceptional innovation, creativity, and impact in their fields. Each year, nominees are evaluated by industry experts, media professionals, and consultants who ensure that only the most deserving candidates receive recognition. About Intensity Therapeutics Intensity is a late-stage clinical biotechnology company whose novel engineered chemistry enables aqueous cytotoxic-containing drug formulations to mix and saturate a tumor's dense, high-fat, pressurized environment following direct intratumoral injection. As a result of the saturation, Intensity's clinical trials have demonstrated the ability of INT230-6 to kill tumors and elicit an adaptive immune response within days of injection, representing a new approach to cancer cell death that holds the potential to shift the treatment paradigm and turn many deadly cancers into chronic diseases even for malignancies that do not respond to conventional immunotherapy. Intensity has completed two clinical studies that enrolled over 200 patients using INT230-6: a Phase 1/2 dose escalation study in metastatic cancers including sarcomas (NCT03058289), and a Phase 2 randomized control clinical trial in locally advanced breast cancer (the "INVINCIBLE-2 Study") (NCT04781725) in women without undergoing chemotherapy prior to their surgery. The Company initiated a Phase 3 trial in soft tissue sarcoma (the "INVINCIBLE-3 Study") (NCT06263231), testing INT230-6 as second or third-line monotherapy compared to the SOC with overall survival as an endpoint. Intensity also initiated a Phase 2 study in collaboration with The Swiss Group for Clinical Cancer Research, formerly SAKK, now the Swiss Cancer Institute (the "INVINCIBLE-4 Study") (NCT06358573) as part of a Phase 2/3 program evaluating INT230-6 followed by the SOC immunochemotherapy and the SOC alone for patients with presurgical triple-negative breast cancer. The pathological complete response rate is the endpoint. summary: EDMONTON, Alberta and NEW YORK, April 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TSX, NYSE:STN Stantec, a global leader in sustainable design and engineering, released its 19th annual Sustainability Report, showcasing how sustainability is integrated into the Company’s strategy, growth, and operations.
body_text: Stantec releases 19th annual Sustainability Report, highlighting 68% (C$5.5 billion) in sustainability-driven revenue 04/21/2026 PDF Version EDMONTON, Alberta and NEW YORK, April 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TSX, NYSE:STN Stantec, a global leader in sustainable design and engineering, released its 19th annual Sustainability Report , showcasing how sustainability is integrated into the Company’s strategy, growth, and operations. The report details Stantec’s sustainability practices, contributions, and accomplishments for the year ending December 31, 2025. The firm’s 2025 sustainability milestones include: C$5.5 billion in revenue from work that supports the United Nations’ core Sustainable Development Goals, representing 68 percent of total gross revenue. This reflects steady growth since the Company began tracking this work in 2019, when it represented 43 percent of total gross revenue. Global operational carbon neutrality achieved for the fourth consecutive year, with continued progress toward net zero emissions under Canada’s Net Zero Challenge, an effort to help the country move toward a cleaner economy Recognition by the Carbon Disclosure Project, earning an A- score for the eighth straight year for demonstrating consistent climate action “The choices we make today shape communities, economies, and the environment of tomorrow,” said Gord Johnston , president and chief executive officer of Stantec. “This is why sustainability is embedded into everything we do—guiding how we live, move, work, and connect. By putting people first, we’re helping create a more resilient and sustainable environment where communities can thrive for generations to come.” The report also brings Stantec’s impact to life through projects that demonstrate how sustainability translates into real-world outcomes: Canada: Advancing cleaner, smarter manufacturing, Stantec supported Duravit’s new facility in Québec— one of the world’s first carbon-neutral manufacturing facilities in the hygienic ceramic industry . Stantec’s building engineering services enabled hydro-powered electric kilns, reducing emissions by nearly 9,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually. United States: In the Klamath Basin of Oregon and California, one of the nation’s largest restoration efforts is revitalizing ecosystems and reconnecting communities. Working alongside Indigenous Nations and local partners, Stantec’s engineers and ecologists are restoring five fish-bearing tributaries, nearly 3.4 miles (5.5 kilometers) of stream channel, 2,200 acres (890 hectares) of native vegetation, and more than 400 miles (644 kilometers) of salmon habitat. United Kingdom: Supporting the transition to cleaner, more reliable energy, the Vyrnwy Frankton Grid Connection in Mid-Wales enables new wind-generated electricity to reach the national grid . Stantec contributed early planning and design for the overhead line, substation, and underground cable infrastructure. New Zealand: Following severe flooding and landslides that damaged over 311 miles (500 kilometers) of roads , Stantec partnered with the Marlborough District Council to shape a future access survey. The study engaged more than 1,500 participants through workshops, hui (gatherings), surveys, webinars, and community events—ensuring local voices informed long-term resilience planning. Egypt: Protecting freshwater resources and expanding access to sanitation, Stantec supported the design of eight wastewater treatment plants around Lake Qarun in the Fayoum region. The project aims to increase access to safe sanitation from 33 percent to 70 percent during the first phase, benefiting approximately 700,000 people while safeguarding the lake’s ecosystem. Stantec’s Sustainability Report is compliant with the Global Reporting Initiative and the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board. title: AI Test updates: synthetic users with SUS scoring and more
summary: Synthetic users now run a built-in System Usability Scale survey, frame previews go full-screen during setup, and AI test runs are more reliable end-to-end.
body_text: Back to updates April 28, 2026 • Product Updates AI Test updates: synthetic users with SUS scoring and more Synthetic users now run a built-in System Usability Scale survey, frame previews go full-screen during setup, and AI test runs are more reliable end-to-end. A few updates to AI tests this month — most notably, you can now get a quantitative usability score out of every test run with synthetic users. Synthetic users with SUS scoring You can now run a SUS (System Usability Scale) survey automatically on the synthetic users you generate for an AI test. SUS is the standard 10-question usability questionnaire that produces a 0–100 score — well-known, widely benchmarked, and useful for comparing designs against each other or against historical baselines. Opt in to SUS during AI test creation. The standard 10 SUS questions are pre-populated and editable Auto-generated responses at the end of every synthetic test run, so SUS becomes part of the same flow as the rest of the test Aggregate scoring in the report — the test results page surfaces the 0–100 score, per-question averages, and sentiment alongside everything else Per-respondent detail when you want to see how each synthetic user rated the experience This is most useful when you want a quick directional signal on a design before putting it in front of real users. Run the AI test, get a SUS score, iterate, run it again, compare. The methodology matches a live SUS survey, so the numbers are comparable to the SUS scores you collect from real participants later. Full-screen frame previews When setting up an AI test against Figma frames or uploaded images, you can now click any thumbnail to open it full-screen. Hover any frame to see the maximize button; press Esc to close. Small but useful when you have several similar-looking frames in a test and need to confirm exactly which one you're attaching to a question. More reliable AI test runs We've made AI test runs more resilient to upstream model issues. Runs now recover automatically from rate limits and transient errors instead of failing partway through. There's no UI for any of this — but if you've had test runs fail intermittently in the past, you should see fewer of those. Sign up today and start running research in minutes. Eric Li , Co-Founder, Versive
